audit_findings.title: Pre-EPP earnings are paired with a post-EPP capital structure
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt increased $1.468 billion from March 31 to June 26, 2026; Q1 total interest expense increased $9 million year over year; EPP purchase consideration was $1.187 billion; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE numerator omits EPP earnings, maintenance capital expenditure and most acquisition financing costs, while the bridge and share denominator reflect the post-acquisition company. Because debt principal is not deducted, incremental interest must reduce equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 31, 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of approximately $2.3 billion and bank and other borrowings of approximately $3.7 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter and timing mismatch. Omitting acquired earnings understates value, while omitting incremental interest, integration costs and maintenance capital expenditure overstates it. The $1.468 billion debt increase is twice the $733.7 million OE anchor, so the unresolved net effect is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE using post-EPP trailing results or a complete EPP pro forma covering acquired earnings, incremental interest, taxes, integration costs and maintenance capital expenditure, then rerun all scenarios with a date-consistent bridge and diluted share count.

audit_findings.title: Historical Nextracker cash-flow add-backs do not match continuing operations
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (FY2024 discontinued-operations operating cash flow was $317 million and parent-attributable discontinued income was $134 million)
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A, working-capital movements, capital expenditure or NCI adjustments enter historical OE even though the income-statement starting point is continuing operations; the contaminated history affects the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The historical statements of comprehensive income and cash flows and the balances related to stockholders’ equity have not been revised to reflect the effect of the spin-off.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated basis mismatch, not merely a possible risk. The filings expressly state that historical cash flows were not revised for the spin-off, while income was retrospectively separated. The direction cannot be determined without continuing-only components, but the filed $317 million discontinued-operations operating cash flow is 43% of the $733.7 million anchor and demonstrates potentially material scale.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2023 and FY2024 OE entirely from continuing-operations, Flex-parent cash flows, including continuing-only D&A, working capital, maintenance capital expenditure and NCI attribution; recompute the trend and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include customer-funded operating capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.7 billion of customer working-capital advances versus $2.840 billion cash; advances equal 59.9% of cash, $4.45 per diluted share and 12.9% of base equity value if fully overlapping
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds gross cash as a non-operating asset even though customer advances may fund cash or operating working capital and remain claims tied to production or termination.
audit_findings.evidence: Customer working capital advances were $ 1.6 billion and $ 2.2 billion, as of March 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence and scale of the advances are demonstrated, but the amount overlapping with bridge cash is unresolved. The $1.7 billion comparison is not itself an adjustment; it shows that the possible misclassification is large enough to materially alter the $34.40 base value even though it would not close the gap to the $109.51 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 cash balance to customer advances, deferred revenue, restricted cash and minimum operating cash; rerun the bridge using only cash demonstrably separable from operations.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings precede a known recurring tax increase
audit_findings.mechanism: A recurring Pillar Two cash-tax burden would reduce normalized OE and every forecast and terminal cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: However, Singapore (our parent company jurisdiction) has enacted OECD Pillar 2 legislation which will be applicable to our fiscal year 2026, which we believe will adversely impact our effective tax rate.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing issue is real because the $733.7 million anchor ends with FY2025, before Pillar Two was reflected. However, FY2026 reported a 23.0% effective rate versus 18.1% in FY2025 while stating that Pillar Two itself was not material, and Q1 FY2027 states that all estimated Pillar Two effects were included in the annual rate. The filings do not isolate its recurring dollar effect, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Pillar Two-specific FY2026 and FY2027 cash-tax amounts by jurisdiction, separate them from settlements and disposition taxes, normalize for the CPI separation, and rerun OE if the recurring amount is material.

audit_findings.title: Nextracker separation leaves a contingent tax claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Any Flex-retained tax or indemnification payment is a contingent claim on equity that is absent from OE and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: If, notwithstanding the conclusions expressed in the private letter ruling and the opinion, the Distributions or the Mergers were determined to be taxable, we, our subsidiaries and our former shareholders could incur significant tax liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The continuing dispute and potential Flex obligation are filed facts, but neither the probability nor maximum retained exposure is supplied. The filing says an adverse outcome could be material, so the risk cannot be dismissed, yet the record cannot demonstrate that it presently changes value materially.
audit_findings.action: Review the Tax Matters Agreement and current dispute record for allocation, indemnification limits, reserves, asserted amounts and probability; add an expected or scenario-weighted claim to the bridge only after those amounts are established.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may carry repatriation taxes
audit_findings.magnitude: $82 million estimated unrecognized deferred-tax liability on $930 million of indefinitely reinvested earnings; additional latest withholding exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Withholding or repatriation taxes reduce the portion of gross cash that can be distributed or redeployed for shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: Although substantially all of the amounts held outside of Singapore could be repatriated, under current laws, a significant amount could be subject to income tax withholdings.
audit_findings.explanation: The known $82 million estimate equals about $0.21 per diluted share and 0.6% of the $13.148 billion base equity value, which alone is not material. However, 29% of June 2026 cash, approximately $824 million, was held by foreign subsidiaries outside Singapore, and the filing does not quantify the total after-tax distributable amount. The broader bridge exposure therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Map June 2026 cash by jurisdiction and legal entity, identify recognized and unrecognized withholding liabilities and indefinitely reinvested balances, and rerun the bridge with after-tax distributable cash.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Residual D&A: FY2017 $96.0 million, FY2018 $42.3 million, FY2019 $257.1 million, FY2021 $85.0 million and FY2024 $39.0 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A shown to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to historical OE, potentially increasing the trend-derived anchor and projected value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2017 $96.0m (15.8% of filed D&A); FY2018 $42.3m (7.6% of filed D&A); FY2019 $257.1m (33.6% of filed D&A); FY2021 $85.0m (14.9% of filed D&A); FY2024 $39.0m (7.3% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No overstatement is demonstrated because the current treatment leaves the unidentified amounts as expenses. Eligibility remains unresolved, and the amounts range from 5.3% to 35.0% of the $733.7 million anchor, so the record cannot establish that the potential understatement is immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Obtain filed component-level D&A classifications for each affected year, identify amounts that are genuinely non-economic and not offset by maintenance capital expenditure, recompute historical OE and rerun the trend only for supported reclassifications.
